newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Soaring U.S. trade gap hits dlr, shares down.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Soaring U.S. trade gap hits dlr, shares down.

text.p: News that the U.S. trade deficit has surged to its highest level in more than eight years caused a wave of selling on Wednesday, sending the dollar below 110 yen and 1.51 marks. The Commerce Department said soaring imports, including costlier foreign oil, caused the shortfall on trade with the rest of the world in July to shoot up 42.6 percent to $11.68 billion -- far above the $8.8 billion forecast by Wall Street economists. The deficit was the highest since late 1987.

Prior to the trade news, the currency markets had been moribund, with the dollar stuck in a tight range around levels seen late on Tuesday. Talk of a possible U.S. Federal Reserve rate rise was completely dominating transactions.

This followed comments on Tuesday by an unnamed Fed official to Reuters that eight of the 12 district banks in the Federal Reserve System have requested a rise in the 5.0 percent discount rate. The Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meets on September 24 and while the market has changed its mind several times about the likelihood of a rate rise, it now believes one is definitely in the offing.

Traders said the market was wary because of the wild swings in sentiment of late and investors were not willing to commit cash until they saw some hard figures. "This really has stirred up a hornets nest," said David Coleman, chief economist at CIBC Wood Gundy. "The big ticket is the talk of a discount rate rise and it's that which is spooking people."
Analysts said that if the discount rate was raised it would suggest that the trend of U.S. rates had decisively turned, with serious implications for investors.
The official release on Wednesday of the extensively-leaked French budget had little effect on the franc. It retreated just over a centime from six-week highs at 3.3957 per mark set on Tuesday.

On the European bourses, leading shares were all lower after the renewed U.S. rate jitters put the brakes on Wall Street's recent surge. Sentiment was further mauled when New York stocks opened mixed on Wednesday and fell again. The Dow Jones Industrial Average was about 20 points down by 1400 GMT.
On the London stock market, analysts said the rate hiatus would mean investors would be wary of pushing ahead very far in coming days
Stronger-than-expected British retail sales early in the day pushed down government bonds and stocks, though analysts said the figures were not likely to have much impact on monetary policy.
"Trading is quiet, People don't think the retail sales numbers are going to change very much and it was really just an excuse to mark the market lower," said one senior trader.
The blue chip FTSE 100 index increased its losses during the day and was about 16 points down shortly the Wall Street open.

In Frankfurt, German shares ended what was described as listless bourse trade slightly lower. Dealers said the market was consolidating after its recent run-up to record levels. Gains were capped by U.S. developments but shares were underpinned by a firmer German debt market and stable dollar.
On the Paris bourse, stocks opened down and continued to trade in negative territory. Dealers said although the market was weaker on the U.S. rate worries, it was still well supported.
One bright point was Alcatel Alsthom, higher after announcing bid to buy Thomson SA and turn it into European defence leader.

On the energy market, traders said oil prices were likely to stay firm for the rest of the year even if the military confrontation between Iraq and the United States was defused, thanks to bullish supply-demand fundamentals.

Lingering concerns over tight heating oil stocks approaching the winter and an indefinite delay to the UN's Iraqi oil-for- food arrangement should keep world benchmark North Sea Brent blend over $20 a barrel for the next few weeks, they said.
CURRENCIES AT 1400 GMT
The dollar was at 1.5086 marks and 109.05 yen compared with 1.5147 marks and 110.35 yen late in Europe on Tuesday .
STOCK MARKETS AT 1400 GMT
The Financial Times-Stock Exchange index of 100 leading British shares had fallen 16.9 points to 3,955.4.
In Paris, the CAC-40 share index dropped 8.97 to 2,071.89.
The 30-share DAX index in Frankfurt closed down 2.38 at 2,625.70
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold fixed easier at $383.00 against $383.55 at Tuesday's London close. Silver was a touch firmer at $5.08.
